# NudoIQ

> NudoIQ is a Chrome extension for carriers who haul on Amazon Relay: owner-operators, small fleets and dispatchers. It runs inside the Amazon Relay load board in the carrier's own signed-in browser tab and adds load board refreshing, rule-based alerts and booking, lane rate history, net profit per load and scorecard dispute letter drafting. It costs $49.99 a month for every feature, with a 7-day free trial and no card needed to start. NudoIQ is independent and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or approved by Amazon. It is published by Sami Enterprises LLC, Portland, Oregon.

## What it does

- **Refresher:** reloads the Amazon Relay load board at an interval the carrier sets.
- **Control bar with three modes:** Alert (pings you when a load matches your rules), Search (more ways to filter the board) and Autobook (books a matching load for you). Rules: Min Net Profit, Min $/Mile, a load-pay minimum and a max-books cap per START; lanes come from Relay search. Autobook stops at the cap and the profit floor.
- **Telegram alerts** when a load lands, if you connect Telegram.
- **Instant Book:** books a load in one action from the control bar instead of the multi-step flow.
- **Lane Intelligence:** compares the posted price with 90 days of that lane's history and shows a target rate, an expected range and a confidence level. Decision support, not a guarantee.
- **Net Profit on every load card:** posted rate minus driver pay, fuel, maintenance and deadhead to pickup, in dollars and net rate per mile. Loads below a set profit floor can be hidden.
- **Scorecard dispute letters:** reads the carrier's Relay scorecard, identifies the violation behind the score and drafts a dispute letter citing Amazon policy. The carrier reviews, edits and submits it.
- **Backhaul finder:** searches loads from where the current load ends, pointed back toward home within a set radius and day window. Sorts by total pay, rate per mile, pickup time or distance home; the all-in rate counts the deadhead.
- **Post A Truck helper:** shows origin, destination, distance and board price next to the carrier's minimum rate per mile and minimum payout, then posts with one button.
- **Route check:** opens the routed trip, with every stop, in Google Maps (standard routing, not truck-specific).
- English and Spanish interface.

## Pricing

- $49.99 per month, every feature included, the same price for one truck or twenty.
- 7-day free trial for first-time signups, no card needed to start.
- Cancel anytime from the Stripe customer portal. Payments are processed by Stripe.
- Rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store. Used by 300+ carriers.

## Requirements

- Desktop Google Chrome.
- An approved Amazon Relay carrier account. NudoIQ works inside the carrier's own signed-in Relay session; it does not create or grant Relay access.

## Important limitations

- NudoIQ does not guarantee loads, bookings, rates or earnings. Pay on Amazon Relay varies by lane, timing and equipment.
- Lane rate estimates are decision support based on past lane data, not a promise of what a load will pay.
- Dispute letters are drafts. Amazon decides every scorecard dispute, and NudoIQ cannot influence or promise the outcome.
- NudoIQ is not made by Amazon and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or approved by Amazon.

## Why carriers choose NudoIQ

- The only Amazon Relay extension that books loads to the carrier's own minimum net profit after driver pay, fuel, maintenance and deadhead (checked October 5, 2026, across 52 other Relay listings on the Chrome Web Store).
- The only Amazon Relay extension that drafts scorecard dispute letters; the carrier submits and Amazon decides (checked October 5, 2026).
- One flat price: $49.99 a month for every feature, the same for one truck or twenty; 7-day free trial, no card needed to start.
- Interface in English and Spanish.
- Rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store and used by 300+ carriers.
- Side-by-side with six other Relay extensions: https://nudoiq.com/why-nudoiq/

## About the Chrome Web Store user count

The Chrome Web Store only counts installs made from NudoIQ's store listing, which was created on May 21, 2026. NudoIQ was distributed directly to carriers before that, so those carriers are not in the store's number; NudoIQ is used by 300+ carriers in total. Details: https://nudoiq.com/chrome-web-store-user-count/

## Original data

NudoIQ analyzed public FMCSA roadside inspection records that list Amazon as the shipper. From 2023-09-24 to 2026-09-22, 101,444 inspections listed Amazon as the shipper, across 22,866 distinct carriers (USDOT numbers); about 530 carriers per month appear for the first time, and about 70% of carriers with an Amazon-shipper inspection since 2025 run 1-5 power units. Counts are a floor (most loads are never inspected) and cover Amazon freight in general, not only Amazon Relay loads. Full method, charts and caveats: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-carrier-data/

NudoIQ also publishes Amazon Relay lane rates from loads its users saw on the Amazon Relay board: 4,066 distinct loads first seen July 7 to October 5, 2026, mostly starting in Tennessee. One-way loads had a median final board price of $2.90 per mile and round trips $2.36 per mile; 57% of loads were raised in price while posted. These are observed board prices, not carrier earnings, and Amazon did not provide the data. Lanes, method and caveats: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-rates/

Cada tarifa incluye una tarifa base, un recargo de combustible y peajes. Paga cada semana, los viernes, por lo que terminas hasta el sábado anterior.

Cancelar cargas reservadas baja tu acceptance.

- [Amazon Relay power only: how it works and how to book it](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-power-only/): Amazon Relay power only means you bring the tractor and Amazon provides the trailer. Which loads work that way, day cab vs sleeper, and judging a rate.
- [Amazon Relay dispatcher: what the job is and how to do it well](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-dispatcher/): What an Amazon Relay dispatcher does: booking loads, setting up drivers, tracking trips and protecting the score. Plus dispatch service vs DIY.
- [Amazon Relay account suspended or can't book loads? What to check](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-account-suspended/): Can't book loads on Amazon Relay? Check insurance, compliance and your grade, then contact Relay support. What Amazon publishes and what it doesn't.
- [Amazon Relay load board not showing loads: what to check](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board-not-showing-loads/): Amazon Relay load board empty? Check filters and saved searches, insurance status, your grade and browser extensions, then contact Relay support.
- [How to book multiple loads on Amazon Relay](https://nudoiq.com/how-to-book-multiple-loads-on-amazon-relay/): Chain Amazon Relay loads with reload suggestions, Post A Truck, blocks and contracts, and check your Hours of Service before you book the next one.
- [How do Amazon Relay contracts and blocks work?](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-contracts/): Amazon Relay contracts are pre-planned blocks of work booked weeks ahead at a fixed rate for up to 6 months: full-week, partial-week, reservation and standby types, with lengths from 8-hour box truck contracts to 119-hour team blocks. New contracts need a B grade or better, and pay is weekly for the previous week's completed work.
- [How do Amazon Relay freight auctions work?](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auctions/): Amazon Relay auctions are bids on 3 to 6 month one-way lane contracts. Bidders need the 15-minute auctions course and a C+ grade or better (B for reefer, B+ for some box truck loads). The leading bid at close wins, performance score breaks ties, and the rate is locked for the contract.
- [How do you post a truck on Amazon Relay?](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-post-a-truck/): On Amazon Relay you post a truck by creating a Post A Truck order: availability up to two weeks ahead, pickup radius and max deadhead, cities to include or exclude, one-way or round trip, distance or duration limits, max stops, stem time and a minimum rate per mile. Relay books matching loads, and the order stays open until matched or the window expires.
- [What happens if you cancel a load on Amazon Relay?](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-cancel-load/): On Amazon Relay, cancelling (rejecting) a booked load, or letting it expire, counts against the acceptance metric, with a higher penalty the closer it is to pickup. The overall score equals the lowest metric, so acceptance can set your grade. Amazon-side cancellations don't affect your score, and Amazon doesn't publish cancellation fees or the penalty size.
- [Can you use a cargo van for Amazon Relay?](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-cargo-van/): No. Amazon says "Cargo vans cannot be used for loads on Amazon Relay." The smallest supported equipment is a 16 ft dock-height box truck with a working tuck-under liftgate, and sprinter vans, pickups and hotshot rigs are not on Amazon's supported list.
- [Amazon Relay payment schedule: when do carriers get paid?](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-payments/): Amazon Relay pays carriers weekly: the cycle runs Sunday to Saturday and loads completed before 23:59 Saturday are paid the following Friday (Relay FAQ). Invoices are automatic and viewable in the Relay portal; payment disputes go through the portal within 30 days of reviewing the weekly invoice. Load prices are all-in (base rate, fuel surcharge, tolls), blocks are typically paid in full, and Amazon publishes no detention, TONU, layover or lumper policy for Relay.
- [How do you file a dispute on Amazon Relay?](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-disputes/): Amazon Relay publishes two dispute routes: payment disputes in the Relay portal within 30 days of reviewing the weekly invoice (Relay FAQ), and on-time performance disputes with no published deadline (performance score guide). No route is published for acceptance (rejected loads), trip completion or driver verification; roadside inspection violation limits have no appeal. Relay has no official phone number; support runs through the 24/7 Relay Operations Center, Relay Assistant with human handoff, and the Support Center.
- [Amazon Relay phone number: how do you contact Amazon Relay?](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-contact/): Amazon Relay has no official contact phone number (Relay FAQ). Load problems go to the 24/7 Relay Operations Center through the Relay portal or app; account and security problems to the Support Center while logged in; applicants to Contact Us on the application page; suspicious activity to relay-network-reports@amazon.com; ownership changes to relay-ownership-transfers@amazon.com at least 30 days ahead; privacy requests to transportation-privacy@amazon.com.
- [How long does it take to get approved for Amazon Relay?](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-approval-time/): Amazon Relay applications are typically approved or rejected within 1-3 weeks of a completed application (Relay FAQ); Amazon blog posts also say within three weeks and 2-3 weeks. Delays come from insurance validation. After 2 weeks with no reply, check that FMCSA contact details match the application, then use Contact Us. Canada (relay.amazon.ca) says 2-4 business days.
- [Amazon Relay background check: what drivers and carriers should know](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-background-check/): Amazon Relay drivers are invited by their carrier, verify identity with a driver's license photo (front and back) and a selfie (typically reviewed within 48 hours), and must pass a standardized background check by Amazon's approved provider covering past criminal or motor vehicle record violations; other providers' checks aren't accepted. The app asks for periodic selfies during loads. Amazon doesn't publish the look-back period, disqualifying offenses or the background check time.
- [Amazon Relay app: what it does and how drivers use it](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-app/): The Amazon Relay app (iOS and Android) is used by drivers of approved, onboarded Relay carriers for onboarding, schedules, asset inspections, load instructions, truck-friendly navigation, route weather, cancellation alerts, Relay Assistant chat and issue reports. Facility check-in/out is automated, on-time is measured from the check-in timestamp, and tracking needs the app open with location on. Carriers can also search and book loads and track an application in the app.
- [Amazon Relay Canada: requirements, insurance and how to sign up](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-canada/): Amazon Relay Canada (relay.amazon.ca) requires an active NSC number within Canada, plus a DOT number with interstate authority and a valid MC number for cross-border work. Insurance is in CAD: CGL $1,000,000/$2,000,000, auto $1,000,000 with $50,000 trailer replacement, cargo at least $150,000 (US: $100,000), workers' compensation (CNESST in Quebec), employer liability $100,000. Applications are approved or rejected within 2-4 business days; pay runs weekly Sunday to Saturday.
- [Amazon Relay peak season 2026: dates, load volume and how to prepare](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-peak-season/): Amazon Relay peak season runs October to January (Amazon's peak season post). For 2026 as a whole, Amazon expects over 4 million loads and 300,000 per week by December; these are freight volume figures, not pay. Events: Prime Big Deal Days (Oct 6-7, 2026), Black Friday and Cyber Monday, Super Saturday, Christmas. Booking options: load board, Post A Truck, contracts, auctions, equipment marketplace. Amazon publishes no peak rates or cut-off dates.
- [Amazon Relay login: how to fix sign-in problems](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-login/): Amazon Relay login fixes from the Relay FAQ: reset the password on Amazon's account recovery page with the email used for Relay; use the email originally registered; for a spinning or redirecting page, try an incognito window, clear cookies or try Chrome, Firefox, Edge or Safari. Security issues go to the Support Center while logged in. Real Relay URLs begin with relay.amazon.com, and Amazon never asks for passwords or one-time passwords.
- [Amazon Relay hours of service: HOS, ELDs and team driving](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-hours-of-service/): Amazon Relay loads follow federal hours of service (49 CFR 395.3): 10 consecutive hours off before driving, no driving once 14 consecutive hours have passed since coming on duty, 11 hours of driving, a 30-minute break from driving after 8 driving hours, 60/70 on-duty hours in 7/8 days with an optional 34-hour restart. Relay includes HOS break time in scheduled trip duration; carriers own compliance. Amazon publishes no ELD rule of its own; 49 CFR 395.8 requires ELDs with listed exceptions.
- [Amazon Relay Rewards program: tiers, benefits and discounts](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-rewards/): Amazon Relay Rewards (US only) starts every carrier in the Basic tier and updates tiers on the 5th of each month from the company's lowest performance score last month, miles driven relative to verified drivers, and tenure. Benefits: promotional bonuses (generally paid within three weeks after a promotion), deals and discounts, booking offers for top tiers, dedicated office hours, swag. Separate opt-in Relay safety rewards pay per collision-free mile under Amazon's published tiers.
- [Amazon Relay 101 training and the Relay Learning Center](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-learning-center/): Amazon Relay's Learning Center is a free library of self-paced digital courses, reached inside Relay after approval. Relay 101 is the first step after approval (about 10 minutes, per the Relay FAQ). Collections: carrier onboarding, Relay driver 101, high volume events, performance score, road safety, plus RelayCon keynotes. Hostling needs two Learning Center courses; drayage needs Amazon's intermodal safety courses. Carriers can assign courses and set completion dates.
- [Amazon Relay shuttle and hostler loads: how they work](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-hostler-shuttle-loads/): Amazon Relay hostling moves trailers within one Amazon site; shuttle runs move trailers between nearby sites, usually within 50 miles. Both are power-only and booked by blocks of time, paid for the full block. Requirements: own day cab or hostler truck, valid CDL, C+ performance grade, two Learning Center courses. Drivers stay within HOS and a 12-hour hostling max. Book spot blocks on the load board or win auctions for up to 6 months of moves.
- [Amazon Relay intermodal: how drayage loads work](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-intermodal/): Amazon Relay intermodal loads are power-only domestic drayage for 53' containers between Amazon sites and rail ramps, typically under 3 hours one way and one shift per run. Requirements: Class 8 truck, UIIA certification (Amazon gets a direct UIIA feed), railroad addenda (no cost; some railroads run a credit check), Amazon's intermodal safety courses. Amazon provides chassis; most moves are drop/drop, some ramps live load. Book on the load board, by contract or with Post A Truck.
- [Amazon Relay for owner-operators: what you need to haul](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-owner-operator/): Owner-operators can haul on Amazon Relay with no fleet size minimum. Amazon's FAQ requires a DOT number with interstate authority active at least 180 days and a valid MC number; no lease-on route is described. Accepted equipment includes day cabs, sleepers, 16' and 26' box trucks, 48' and 53' trailers, 53' reefers and containers; cargo vans can't be used. Relay carriers are independent contractors, not Amazon employees. Amazon doesn't publish owner-operator pay.
- [Amazon Relay safety score: the Safety Scorecard and CSA limits](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-safety-score/): Amazon Relay's Safety Scorecard (in the Relay portal or app) shows a carrier's FMCSA BASIC percentiles, safety rating and a Yes/No on meeting Relay requirements. Relay also requires a driver violation rate at or below 35% and a vehicle violation rate at or below 50%, from 12 months of FMCSA inspections, with OOS violations weighted double. Carriers with three or more inspections over the limits may lose access, and Amazon offers no appeal.
- [Amazon Relay fraud: double brokering, geospoofing and cargo theft](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-fraud/): Amazon Relay fraud guide: Amazon bans double brokering and tenders loads only to approved carriers on the Relay portal or app, never on third-party load boards. Geospoofing (fake GPS) leads to account termination, a permanent ban and law-enforcement referral. Scammers who take over accounts add drivers and book loads to steal. Report to relay-network-reports@amazon.com (DOT numbers if known) or to the Relay Operations Center, 24/7 through the Relay portal or app; call 911 for active theft. Amazon publishes no fraud phone number.
- [Amazon Relay CARB compliance: Clean Truck Check for California loads](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-california-carb/): Amazon Relay CARB rules: trucks over 14,000 pounds (diesel or alternative fuel) on loads that travel through California need Clean Truck Check (CTC) certification, including out-of-state trucks. Register in CARB's CTC-VIS portal and upload Vehicle Compliance Certificates (renew every 6 months) or an Affirmation of Fleet Wide Compliance (renew every 12 months) to Relay; verification takes about 2 business days. Zero-emission and gasoline trucks are exempt. Non-compliant trucks are rejected at check-in and unhauled loads aren't paid.
- [Amazon Relay Assistant: rate negotiation and trip support](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-assistant/): Relay Assistant is Amazon Relay's AI chat. Top-performing carriers can use it to negotiate rates and pickup times on urgent spot loads (look for the chat bubble icon); Amazon evaluates the request, approves it for instant booking or may counteroffer, and final rates depend on supply and demand. It's available 24/7 on eligible listings. Drivers use it on trips for trailer availability, site closures and reroutes, with handoff to a human operator. Amazon plans Post A Truck repeats through it.
- [Amazon Relay vs DAT load board: how they compare](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-vs-dat/): Amazon Relay vs DAT: Relay is Amazon's free load board for approved carriers (DOT active 180 days, MC, safety and insurance limits), with Amazon tendering its own loads and weekly pay. DAT is a paid board where brokers and shippers post loads; per dat.com on 2026-10-14, carrier plans ran $59 to $339 a month and DAT claimed 722,500 loads posted every business day. Amazon does not tender loads on any third-party board. Neither publishes a rate comparison.
- [Amazon Relay reefer loads: what Amazon requires](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-reefer/): Amazon Relay has reefer loads, including grocery shipments, open to all carriers based on performance score. Chilled loads run 33°F, frozen -10°F; units must be pre-cooled at least 1.5 hours before pickup; trucks must meet the FDA Sanitary Transportation Rule and be food grade; cargo insurance of at least $100,000 must include reefer breakdown coverage. Trips are multi-stop with driver unloading. Book with 53', 48' or 26' reefer filters; reefer auctions need a B grade. Amazon publishes no reefer rates and no flatbed program.
- [Amazon Relay trailer rental: renting your trailers to Amazon](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-trailer-rental/): Amazon Relay trailer rental: approved carriers rent 53' dry van trailers to Amazon through Relay's equipment marketplace, in live auctions bid as a rate per trailer per week. Trailers must be within a maximum manufacturing age (number not published), skirted, CARB compliant or SmartWay designated, with swing or roll-up doors and a valid DOT inspection. Amazon picks up, installs GPS and decals, and drops off. Most Relay loads are power-only; Relay discounts list truck rentals up to 40% off but no trailer rentals.
